implementation_notes: The stdlib realization is unittest.mock: Mock(wraps=real) (or patch.object(..., wraps=...)) delegates attribute access and calls to the real object while recording, and the test asserts afterwards with assert_called_once_with/assert_called_with, mock.call_args_list, method_calls or mock_calls - the documented action-then-assertion model rather than record/replay. What replaces the classic spy class is the generic Mock plus patch(), which also restores the original attribute at scope exit; a hand-written recorder is only needed when the collaborator must be a genuine instance (isinstance checks) or when patching would reach too deep into the SUT.
code_sketch:
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

real = Mailer()
spy = MagicMock(wraps=real)          # delegates to the real object
OrderService(spy).place(order)       # real behaviour runs
spy.send.assert_called_once_with('bob@example.com', body)
pitfalls: assert_called_with compares with ==; a mutable argument changed after the call can compare unequal to the recorded snapshot.
A Mock without spec accepts any attribute, so a typo in the asserted method name quietly passes on a child mock - use autospec/spec_set to pin the interface.
patch() must replace the name where the SUT looks it up, not where it is defined, or the real collaborator is still called and the spy records nothing.
